chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of Bakr ibn Salih, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Zayd, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father (peace be upon them) that God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Indeed, the fastest good deed to receive reward is righteousness (al-birr), and indeed, the fastest evil deed to receive punishment is transgression (al-bughy). And sufficient is a person's flaw that he looks at people's faults while being blind to his own, and reproaches people for what he himself cannot abandon, and harms his companion for no reason.

key_terms.الْبُغْيُ: Transgression or exceeding bounds, referring to evil deeds
key_terms.الْبِرُّ: Righteousness or goodness, referring to virtuous deeds

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that are enough to be considered a flaw in a person according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a concise moral diagnostic, linking the Prophet’s teaching on the reciprocity of swift reward for *birr* (righteousness) and swift punishment for *bughya* (transgression) to three specific social vices. The narration emphasizes self-awareness over external judgment, warning against the hypocrisy of criticizing others for flaws one cannot relinquish and the rudeness of imposing one’s own concerns on companions. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and *muhasaba* (self-accounting) as foundational to spiritual integrity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-81 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Bakr ibn Salih, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faz’zal, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Zayd, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “

Indeed the reward of doing good deeds will arrive much sooner than any good deeds, the punishment for doing evil deeds will reach one much faster than any evil deeds. Having three characteristics is enough for one to be bad. These characteristics are: attending to other people’s faults while ignoring your own; admonishing others against evil deeds without being able to abandon them yourself and hurting your companion for nothing.”
